blocks.text: B2-07 · Understanding an interview
Lesson overview

Interviews are one of the richest and most insidious sources: the interviewed person speaks firsthand, but chooses what to say and what to keep quiet, and the journalist chooses what to ask and what to publish. In this unit you learn the genres of the interview (printed, television, radio), the types of question and their purpose, the characteristics of fuṣḥā spoken (falling desires, filling words, self-corrections), the techniques by which an interviewee avoids a question and the way to report precisely what has been said and what has not been said. Four weeks, in parallel with the end of EGY-13 and the beginning of EGY-14.

rows: B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty
20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 182–185), plus the EGY track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, script for vocal synthesis, extracts of radio or television interviews in fuṣḥā (Appendix C), sessions with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize the genres of the interview and their conventions (demand and answer, introduction, title);
2. classify questions (open, closed, in-depth, oriented) and understand what they are looking for;
3. follow the fuṣḥā talk of an interview, with its simplifications and its filling words;
4. recognize when an interviewee does not respond, and how he does so;
5. report an interview with the right verbs, including waste and non-answers ( ⁧رَفَضَ التَّعْلِيقَ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَسْتَبْعِدْ⁩ ).
Four-week plan.

The press conventions. A printed interview usually has: a title with a phrase of the guest in quotes (B1-15); a brief introduction ( ⁧مُقَدِّمَة⁩ ) about who is the guest and why you interview him; then questions and answers. The acronyms often appear ⁧س⁩ ( ⁧سُؤَال⁩ ) e ⁧ج⁩ ( ⁧جَوَاب⁩ ), or the name of the newspaper and guest. Formulas: ⁧أَجْرَى الحِوَارَ⁩ The interview was conducted by the interviewer. ⁧المُحَاوِر⁩ The interviewer is the person who is the interviewer. ⁧فِي حِوَارٍ خَاصٍّ مَعَ⁩ ... ................................ ...in an exclusive interview with....................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................

8. Pronunciation and Prosody

The break. In fuṣḥā spoken almost every group of words ends up in a pausing form, without desinence: ⁧نَحْنُ نَعْمَلُ عَلَى هٰذَا المَشْرُوع⁩ ( -ʿ end without vowel) · ⁧مُنْذُ ثَلَاثِ سَنَوَات⁩ . Practice reading Script B this way: it's more natural than with all terminations. The intonation of the questions. ⁧هَلْ⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ and closed questions go up to the end; questions with ⁧مَا⁩ , ⁧كَيْفَ⁩ , ⁧مَتَى⁩ descend; ⁧أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنَّ⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ It is almost a yes tone, which goes down: it is a question that wants a yes.
9. New lexicon

Notes of use. ⁧أَجَابَ عَنْ⁩ and ⁧رَدَّ عَلَى⁩ both mean "responder" (s); ⁧رَدَّ عَلَى⁩ is more frequent when responding to a criticism or accusation ( ⁧رَدَّ عَلَى مُنْتَقِدِيهِ⁩ ). ⁧اِسْتَبْعَدَ⁩ has also the concrete sense "Exclude someone" ( ⁧اُسْتُبْعِدَ مِنَ الفَرِيقِ⁩ The team was excluded from the team, but in interviews it is almost always unlikely to be: ⁧لَا أَسْتَبْعِدُ⁩ • not excluded, i.e. it is possible (B2-09).
